issues.description: PR bundles three unrelated changes: README restyle, example behavior change, and new tests.
issues.detail: Title says 'add POST tests' but the diff also rewrites README.rst formatting and swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read() in things_advanced.py. These are three separable patches that should be split for reviewability and bisectability. Land tests, the example fix with rationale, and the README cleanup as separate commits.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is an unexplained semantic change.
issues.detail: PR description says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the diff swaps the stream identity entirely. bounded_stream and stream have different IO semantics. Either justify why bounded_stream is correct here in the commit message or revert. This is a behavior change motivated by making a test pass, not a documented fix.

issues.description: README silently flips StorageError.handle signature from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params).
issues.detail: Falcon's error handler signature is API-load-bearing and the README is copy-paste material. Flipping argument order inside a diff sold as formatting cleanup is exactly how downstream users break. Either land the change as its own deliberate commit with rationale, or revert.

issues.description: FAQ test exercises header-body mismatch rather than the empty-body invariant it appears to test.
issues.detail: The test sends body='' with Content-Length: '1' and asserts 400, complecting 'empty body' with 'lying Content-Length header.' Neither the test nor surrounding prose names the invariant being exercised. If the point is empty-body handling, send an empty body honestly; otherwise document what mechanism produces the 400.

issues.description: FAQ example contains a dead branch: `req.content_length or 0` after the None/0 case is already excluded.
issues.detail: The outer guard checks `if req.content_length in (None, 0)`, so in the else branch content_length is guaranteed truthy and the `or 0` fallback is unreachable. In docs example code every token should mean what the reader thinks it means; simplify or delete the redundant expression.

issues.description: New tests and FAQ snippet lack comments, use magic literals, and rely on `assert(...)` footgun shape.
issues.detail: The magic user_id '1337' appears uncommented; resp1-4 bundle independent assertions; `assert(result.status == HTTP_400)` parses as paren-expression and risks the `assert(x, y)` footgun when copied. Add one-line comments naming each invariant, prefer bare `assert x == y`, and consider splitting bundled scenarios.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The PR bundles three separable changes — new POST tests, a semantic swap from req.stream to req.bounded_stream in the example, and a sweeping README restyle that silently flips an error handler argument order — which all three reviewers flag as the central problem. The tests and FAQ addition are reasonable in intent, but the empty-body test exercises a header-body lie rather than the invariant it claims, and the FAQ snippet carries a dead branch and an `assert(...)` footgun that copy-paste readers will inherit. Split the PR into tests-only, example-fix-with-rationale, and README-cleanup commits; justify the bounded_stream switch; name the invariants the tests pin down.
